If positive, find two real solutions using the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / 2a. If zero, there's one solution; if negative, no real solutions exist. Practice makes it easier to understand each step.

Find the derivative f'(x) first. Set it equal to zero and solve for x to get critical points. Plug these back into f''(x). If positive, it's a local minimum; if negative, a maximum.
